title: Keep chat and the token out of a fresh Remote agent: no catch-up, hook-gated delivery, no token in argv
body:
Two defects left by commit bdf3877 (read its body, then docs/remote-sessions.md and the spec's Results). The human has DECIDED both fixes (2026-11-23); build exactly this.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (sections: The way back, Agent state). Read docs/agent-state.md before touching hook events.
Blocked by: Carry the reply note in the prompt so it cannot answer Claude's folder-trust dialog

PART 1. Chat typed into a fresh Remote agent can still answer Claude's folder-trust dialog and quit it.
Seen on the real Remote: a Claude opened with a prompt into an untrusted directory, in a room that already held broadcasts, got them typed as catch-up on its first Ready frame and quit within 6 s. Cause: WindowManager::chat_tick injects through inject_chat once chat_input_available() is true (Ready = first PTY output, agent state None or Idle); a new Member's cursor starts at 0, so chat.rs tick delivers the whole backlog; the trust dialog reports no state.
1a. A Member created for a FIRST launch on a Remote Session starts reading the room at its current end: no catch-up of posts made before it joined. Reconnect keeps the Member and its cursor exactly as today. Local Sessions are unchanged (say why in docs/remote-sessions.md: a local agent has the foreman skills and its catch-up has never raced a dialog foreman cannot see through ssh; keep it to two lines).
1b. 1a alone still loses to a post that arrives while the dialog is up. For a Claude Remote Session (the only one with hooks on a Remote), hold ALL chat injection for a connection until the first hook event of that connection has arrived through the Tunnel. Verify FIRST on the real Remote, in a never-trusted directory, that no hook event arrives while the trust dialog is showing and that one does arrive once it is answered. If the existing events do not give a prompt-less Claude any event until its first turn, try adding SessionStart to the launch hook settings and observe whether it fires only after the dialog is answered (expected: Claude runs no hooks before trust). If no event reliably marks "past the dialog" for both a Claude launched with a prompt and one launched bare, implement 1a only, STOP on 1b, and report exactly what you saw. Held posts must not be lost: they deliver in order once the gate opens. No timeout that opens the gate blind (that would re-create the bug). A reconnect (claude --continue) gets the same gate with its own first event; check that it does get one, or exempt reconnect and say why. Codex, Grok, shells: no gate (no hooks), 1a only. A new hook event must go through the existing /hook route and hook lane and must not change the badge mapping unless docs/agent-state.md says what it maps to.

PART 2. The bearer token must never sit in an agent's command line on the Remote.
bdf3877 appends the reply note, with the literal token, to the prompt argument; every user on the Remote can read it in ps for the agent's whole life and with it post chat as that Member, read history and status, and fake its badge. The launch script already exports FOREMAN_URL and FOREMAN_TOKEN on a Posix Remote, and the hook settings already name them instead of the literals.
2a. The in-prompt note for Claude on a Posix Remote names $FOREMAN_URL and $FOREMAN_TOKEN, never the literals. Verify on the real Remote that Claude's Bash tool sees both variables (the post in the evidence below must be made with them). Keep one source for the command shape (tunnel.rs reply_commands); the two spellings differ only in how URL and token are written.
2b. Everything else never carries the literal in argv: Codex, Grok, and any Windows Remote go back to the typed note at launch (the pre-bdf3877 behaviour), unless you VERIFY on the real Remote that the agent's tool shell sees both variables. Check Codex there (it is installed; do NOT use its hook-trust bypass flag): if its tool shell has FOREMAN_TOKEN it may carry the variable form, if not it gets the typed note. Grok is not installed and no Windows Remote exists: typed note, stated as unverified.
2c. Add a test that fails if any built Remote launch line or argv contains the token literal outside the script's own export (decode the base64 line in the test rather than weakening it). The typed note still shows the literal on screen; that is unchanged and stays documented.
2d. Correct docs/remote-sessions.md and both providers' foreman-dispatch skill copies (embedded-skill rebuild rule in foreman-docs-and-writing) to what is now true, including which agents get the note in the prompt and which get it typed.

Known and NOT in this card: one-word briefs are not recognised as a prompt (remote::prompt_index) and get the typed note; leave prompt_index's rule alone.

Verify on the real Remote. Test Remote: andy@192.168.8.168 (hostname Falador, Debian, key login; never ask for a password). The human has a dev instance running (target/agent/build, target/agent/appdata) with their own Claude Remote Session open in ~/Projects/Android TV Remote on that machine: touch neither, and never kill a claude process on the Remote that you did not start. You run inside the installed foreman, which lacks these changes. Build and run your OWN instance the way bdf3877's worker did: cargo build --release --target-dir target/agent/hooks; config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s already exists with settings.json (Remote named falador) and a workspace.json holding one empty Project, reuse it; launch with APPDATA pointed there and the environment stripped the way scripts/run-dev.ps1 does; drive it through ITS pipe (foreman-ctl-<pid>-*, listed from PowerShell with Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\) with FOREMAN_PIPE set and FOREMAN_PROJECT_ID / FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID unset, using the exe you built as the CLI. Use a NEW never-trusted directory under /tmp for each attempt.
Evidence to capture with snapshot and status --json, timestamps included:
(a) with at least two earlier broadcasts already in the room, a Claude opened with a prompt sits at the trust dialog, nothing typed, alive after 30 s;
(b) a broadcast posted WHILE the dialog is showing is not typed into it, and Claude is still alive 30 s later;
(c) after you answer the dialog with send, the held post is delivered, Claude posts back using $FOREMAN_URL / $FOREMAN_TOKEN, and the room shows it;
(d) on the Remote, `ps -eo args` (or /proc/<pid>/cmdline) for that agent does not contain the token (compare against the token your instance issued; do not print the token in the commit or docs);
(e) Codex: which path it took and why, and that its cmdline has no token.
Then close your Sessions, stop YOUR instance by PID only (never by name), remove your /tmp directories on the Remote, and remove the trust entries your tests added for those /tmp paths from the Remote's ~/.claude.json only if you can do it without touching any other entry (otherwise list them in the report).
Do not: install anything on the Remote; assume foreman, its skills or its hook files exist there; widen what a Remote agent may do (post chat, read history, read status, report hook events; nothing else); change any control-plane request on the wire; stop any foreman by name; ask for a password; mark anything on Grok or a Windows Remote as tested.
Done when:
- a first-launch Remote Member starts at the room's end and a reconnect keeps its cursor (unit tests); local Members unchanged (test)
- the Claude hook gate holds and then releases chat in order (unit tests), or 1b is reported as not buildable with the observation that shows why
- no Remote launch carries the token literal in argv (test 2c), and the per-agent choice of in-prompt versus typed note is a pure function with a table test
- evidence (a) to (e) observed on the real Remote and recorded in the commit body and the spec's Results; anything not shown is named as unverified
- docs and both skill copies say what is true; cite-guard clean; full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
